accepts.because: a turn to screen before it reaches the agent. The caller MUST promote the identity to context.channel, or every surface shares one bucket and is rate-limited as one. context.user_id is the SECOND identity dimension and is OPTIONAL: the sender rules address it by name (field 'user_id'), but the screen reads it as the empty string when nobody promotes it and screens it like any other value -- a dimension with no enabled allow row is unconstrained (RULE 4), and a deny row on the empty string cannot exist because a row without a value is refused as rules_unreadable (RULE 2). The shipped seed's two user_id rows are enabled: 0, so an unpromoted user_id costs a shipped colony nothing. It starts costing the moment an operator enables an allow row on that dimension: from then on every turn without a promoted user_id is rejected with sender_not_allowed / allowlist:user_id. Promote it if this colony has per-user rules -- that is a wiring decision, and this lane will not make it for you

emits.because: the turn survived every rule; this is the only lane into the agent behind it

the turn was refused. hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id say what happened; what to do about it is the parent's decision. One of the reasons is not a rule at all: 'store_refused' (rule_id 'store-refused') means the rules store did not answer, and the screen fails CLOSED on that the way it fails closed on an unreadable rule row -- hop.store_error then carries the store's own error_code and hop.store_operation the refused op (GH #343)

description.purpose: Scope marker of the firewall: bundles the deterministic screen and its rule store behind one entry lane and two exit routes. Every inbound turn of a channel passes it before anything agentic is reached, and leaves either unchanged on 'pass' or refused on 'reject' with the rule that fired named on the hop.
description.use_when: One per ingress channel, between the surface and the agent's intake. Instantiate it in the same mutation that wires the ingress lane and BOTH exits; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No model anywhere -- whether a turn is admissible is decided by comparisons and a clock. No outbound speech: the firewall never answers the sender. No rewriting: a passed turn is byte-identical to the one that arrived.
